pipeline_name: Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al Arab Gas Pipeline

validity.recommendation: Change Status operating -> construction (mechanically complete but idle); blank/flag StartYear2=2025 until gas actually flows. Re-check after the Khor Al-Zubair FSRU commissions (target 1 June 2026).
validity.researcher_notes: STATUS IS WRONG. The physical pipe is real and correctly described: 40 km, 42 in, from Khor Al-Zubair port to the Nazim Shatt al-Arab regulator, built by the Oil Ministry via Oil Projects Company (SCOP) + South Gas Company. Construction began 9 Feb 2025 and finished on schedule in June 2025 - but every source describes it only as 'ready to receive gas' (جاهز لاستلام الغاز), NOT as flowing/operating. Its sole purpose is to carry IMPORTED dry gas (regasified 'Gulf gas' LNG) from the planned Khor Al-Zubair floating LNG platform (FSRU). That FSRU does not exist yet: Iraq only signed the definitive FSRU deal with Excelerate Energy on 28 Oct 2025 (Hull 3407, still under construction in South Korea, commercial ops expected 2026), and the Ministry of Electricity set 1 June 2026 as the deadline to have the platform delivering 500 MMscf/d. So on the sheet's update date (2025-07-15) the pipe was mechanically complete but had NO gas source and could not have been 'operating.' The row's own Status refs corroborate this: the Facebook video and Baghdad Today link were tagged as failing verification because neither says 'operating' - they are groundbreaking/announcement clips, not a commissioning report. This is a completed-but-not-commissioned line; 'operating' overstates it. StartYear2=2025 (operations start) is likewise premature.

validity.recommendation: Keep the entity; fix Status per the concern above and adopt the verified refs staged in fills.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed - multiple independent sources (Shafaq News EN, Azzaman/Iraq edition AR, Iraq Business News, Al-Mirbad, PowerNews) all report the same 40 km / 42 in Khor Al-Zubair -> Nazim Shatt al-Arab dry-gas line begun Feb 2025. Real project, not a phantom. CLASSIFICATION: correct - it is a gas transmission trunk (dry gas, ties into the national dry-gas pipeline), NOT an oil/NGL line and not gathering/plant-internal; none of the GulfPub Iraq crude lines match it. DUPLICATE: none - endpoints (Khor Al-Zubair -> Shatt al-Arab regulator) are distinct from P1850 (Khor Al-Zubair->Hartha), P6824 (Shouibah->Khor Al-Zubair) and P2234 (N.Rumaila->Khor Al-Zubair); no relabel/double-count found in the 36-row roster. ATTRIBUTION: confirmed - Operator = Oil Projects Company/SCOP (شركة المشاريع النفطية) with South Gas Company; Owner = Iraq Ministry of Oil (100%); province Basrah; endpoints Khor Al-Zubair -> Shatt al-Arab regulator; fuel = (imported) dry gas. SPEC: length 40 km, diameter 42 in, capacity 200 MMscf/d all corroborated by >=2 independent sources - note the Arabic 'مقمق' resolves to million standard cubic feet/day (Shafaq EN: 'up to 200 million standard cubic feet per day'), so the GEM unit MMcf/d is correct, NOT million cubic metres.

routes.start_name: Khor Al-Zubair port (planned FSRU jetty), Basrah
routes.end_name: Nazim Shatt al-Arab regulator (tie-in to national dry-gas pipeline), Basrah
routes.corridor_desc: ~40 km line running generally north/north-east from the Khor Al-Zubair port/industrial area (~30.19N, 47.88E - a well-known port, coordinate approximate) through Basrah governorate to the 'Nazim Shatt al-Arab' regulator near Basra, where it ties into the national dry-gas grid feeding Basra-area power plants (Najibiyah, Hartha). END COORDINATE LEFT NULL: sources name the endpoint only as 'ناظم شط العرب' and there is real ambiguity with the Shatt al-Basra regulator; I would not invent a lat/lon. Tightest defensible bound: the terminus lies within the Basra city / lower Shatt al-Arab area roughly 30.4-30.6N, 47.7-47.9E, ~40 km from Khor Al-Zubair.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from named facilities in independent reporting (Khor Al-Zubair port FSRU jetty -> Nazim Shatt al-Arab regulator). Start coordinate is the known Khor Al-Zubair port location (approximate). End coordinate deliberately left null - the 'Nazim Shatt al-Arab' regulator could not be pinned to a defensible lat/lon (name ambiguity vs Shatt al-Basra regulator); no coordinate fabricated. Corridor is a ~40 km bound only, hence suggested low route accuracy for any future routes-repo branch.

summary: P7435 real + correctly classified gas transmission trunk (40 km / 42 in / 200 MMcf/d all corroborated), but STATUS concern: pipe mechanically complete ~June 2025 yet idle - no gas until Khor Al-Zubair FSRU commissions (target June 2026), so 'operating' is premature; recommend construction.
